newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Heavy crudes starting to slip.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Heavy crudes starting to slip.

text.p: The Asian heavy crude market was marginally weaker as buyers were sidelined, preferring to watch how the Japan weather develops before resuming their summer purchases, traders said on Thursday.
"The only buying interest was coming from Japan, as China and all the other buyers were scared off by the rising premiums," said a trader with a Japanese oil company.
"But now even the Japanese buyers are holding back, as the weather in Japan is hot one day and cool the next day."
"The heavy grades are still strong relative to light crudes, but the bull run seems to be winding down." said another trader.
August Minas was talked around ICP +70/75 cents per barrel, compared to earlier discussions of around ICP +80.
August Cossack was sold by a major at Tapis APPI -80, firmer than the last Cossack cargo sold by the same seller at Tapis APPI -1.00.
Some traders saw this as a sign that the light crude prices were rebounding after touching year low levels.
But others said more than adequate supplies could still keep prices weak.
"There is still quite a bit of light sweets available, such as Tapis and Belida" said a trader with a major oil company.
A VLCC of August 18-20 loading Djeno/Nkossa crudes was confirmed sold by a trader to South Korea last week, but interest for West African crude from other Asian buyers was limited.
"China has a high gasoil stocks, so is not interested in West African cargoes." said a western tarder.
A South Korean refiner heard bought August Masila from a trader at Dubai +13, following an earlier purchase at Dubai +9.
Two August Masila cargoes were heard still on offer, but demand was thin as refiners have completed their August programme, traders said. --A. Ahmad, Singapore (+65 870 3082)
